title: peru awaits india response trade talks near end minister says 2026 09 11
text:
LIMA, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Peru is awaiting a response to a counterproposal it sent to India as negotiations for a free trade agreement enter their final stretch, with ​Lima hoping the deal can be signed in 2027, the country's Minister ‌for Trade Rogers Valencia said on Friday.
India has become the second-largest destination for Peruvian exports this year, overtaking the United States, driven mainly by gold shipments, according to official data from the ​ministry.
"Negotiating with India is a fairly lengthy process,” Valencia told Reuters in an interview. "However, ​a counterproposal has now been sent to India, we are finalizing ⁠this process, and we hope the treaty with India can be signed in 2027," ​he added.
China remains Peru's top export partner, fueled mainly by copper and minerals.
Official data ​showed exports to India totaled $6.184 billion between January and July, up 152% from the same period a year earlier, while shipments to the United States reached $5.971 billion, a 21% increase.
India and Peru began their ​first round of free trade agreement negotiations in 2017.
Peru, a leading copper producer, ​expects exports to hit a record high of more than $100 billion this year, up from about $91 billion ‌in ⁠2025, according to Valencia.
Speaking a day after U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to Peru, Valencia said he had discussed higher U.S. duties introduced in July on the country's exports.
"The conversation was very frank and very open, and we noticed a great ​deal of receptiveness from ​Rubio," Valencia said. "I ⁠mentioned that the tariff rate recently imposed by the United States, not only on Peru but on many other countries, would ​affect our exports this year. So this is under negotiation."
While Peru ​has traded ⁠largely tariff-free with the U.S. under a 2009 agreement, the new duties have hit Peru's agricultural exports, specifically blueberries, textiles, grapes and avocados.
Valencia added that he expects to travel to ⁠the ​United States later this month with President Keiko Fujimori ​for the United Nations General Assembly, where Peru hopes to push forward talks with Washington on tariffs ​and bilateral trade relations.
